chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashaar Al-Wasity, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about marriage, so he wrote to me: 'The one who proposes to you, if you are pleased with his religion and his trustworthiness, then marry (your daughter) to him. If you do not, there will be strife in the land and great mischief.'
ai.seo_question: What are the primary criteria for accepting a marriage proposal in Shia jurisprudence according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes religious piety and trustworthiness as the primary criteria for selecting a spouse, reflecting the Shia emphasis on moral integrity over lineage or wealth. The warning of 'fitnah' and 'fasad' underscores the communal consequences of neglecting these criteria, linking individual marital choices to broader social stability.
